adjacent_skills.you_have: C/C++ and CUDA C++ (no stated C++17/20 idiom depth)

adjacent_skills.jd_skill: Safety, security and quality system requirements

required_skills: Safety, security and quality system requirements
key_responsibilities: Write and review modern C++ code to implement new system features
Test features with unit tests and on hardware
Maintain and use Zephyr RTOS features for lower layers of the system
Investigate bugs by analysing logs and traces, root cause and fix
Participate in agile meetings and program increment discussions

strengths: STM32 bare-metal peripheral work is register-level and real: timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, a hand-written low-level I2C driver, and direct GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 programming at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM with a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
RTOS is genuine though narrow: FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination alongside interrupt-driven UART and multi-servo PWM (Object Tracking Turret).

On-hardware testing and bug triage match the JD's day-to-day closely: resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability over 10/10 trials at ~11.5 s end-to-end; AL5B repeatability measured at <2 mm over 10 trials.

Inter-processor communication across a multi-controller system: Jetson-to-STM32 command link over UART, plus a three-layer Flutter / Flask-SocketIO / Jetson+Arduino pipeline over a unified WebSocket fabric.
The degree requirement is met outright twice over (M.S. Computer Engineering, B.E. Electronics and Telecommunication), so the JD's '2+ years if not directly embedded-focused' clause does not bind.
real_gaps: Modern C++ as the JD means it. The C++ on record is Arduino-style embedded C++ (two-link IK on Arduino) and CUDA C++ compute kernels. Nothing shows C++17/20 idiom work, RAII, templates, the standard library, or reviewing someone else's C++.
Unit testing. No test framework, no test suite, no TDD evidence anywhere in the profile. Every testing claim is manual, on-hardware and trial-count based.
Zephyr RTOS. FreeRTOS mutex usage does not carry over to Zephyr's devicetree, Kconfig and driver-model workflow, and the JD puts the lower system layers there.
Log and trace analysis as a tooling discipline. Bug investigation is evidenced by outcome, not by instrumented tracing (no SystemView, no structured logging, no trace capture).
Agile ceremonies and SAFe program increment planning. Zero exposure; low risk for a new grad, but it is a stated responsibility.

Regulated-domain firmware process. A fire alarm system is life-safety hardware under EN 54; the profile shows fail-safe instincts (ToF range gate at 25 mm, motor-halt state machine on controller disconnect) but no certification, hazard analysis or safety-process experience.

Seniority and scope: this is component ownership inside a shipping, certified, 3+ microcontroller product built by a distributed European consultancy team. The profile's scope is capstone, coursework and internship.

Non-skill but decisive in practice: Porto is on-site hybrid and F-1 OPT authorizes work only inside the United States, so the role needs Portuguese work authorization the employer would have to sponsor. The posting says nothing either way.
overstated_by_keywords: 'C++' counted as a clean Have. In reality it splits into Arduino C++ and CUDA C++, neither of which is the modern application C++ this role reviews daily.
'RTOS' counted as a Have on the strength of one project using FreeRTOS mutexes; the JD wants someone maintaining RTOS lower layers.
'Hardware testing' counted as a Have, but the JD pairs it with unit tests and only the hardware half is backed.
understated_by_keywords: Fail-safe system design never string-matched 'safety': the Robocon fail-safe state machine halting all motors on controller disconnect, and the COFFIN dual-ToF gate that blocks a grasp outside 25 mm, are exactly the reflex a fire-alarm team wants.
Multi-controller integration was scored as missing, but COFFIN is a three-node distributed system and the turret is a two-processor Jetson-to-STM32 link over UART.
Firmware resource discipline (3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, deterministic 1 Hz) reads directly on a constrained multi-MCU product.
Interrupt-driven design from first principles: a 4-bit A/B quadrature transition state machine on hardware interrupts, and 15 kHz PWM across four channels.
screening_gaps: Modern C++ depth. This role writes and reviews modern C++ every day and the profile's C++ is embedded-C-with-classes plus CUDA kernels. This is the same depth probe that has cost interviews before, so it breaks first.
No unit testing of any kind. A consultancy selling into regulated health and finance will probe test discipline early, and there is nothing to answer with.
Zephyr and the RTOS depth behind it. The JD parks the lower layers in Zephyr and calls it 'a plus', but one FreeRTOS project will not survive a question about devicetree, Kconfig or writing a driver.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The hardware half of this job is genuinely backed: register-level STM32 peripheral work, interrupt-driven firmware, multi-controller comms, and real on-target debugging of a system that had to work. The software-engineering half is not. Modern C++, unit testing and Zephyr are three of the five stated responsibilities and none has real evidence, which is what a technical screen would find. Worth applying because Zuhlke accepts the degree outright and lists Zephyr only as a plus, but C++ and testing are the gaps to close before the screen, not after.

outcome.notes: Rejected: role requires a valid local work permit (work authorization, not skills).
